result.topic_en: Formula-only calculations on a parabolic equation p u_ββ + q u_β = u_t: differentiating with respect to a parameter α, making coefficients linear/quadratic in α, and substituting u = aα + b to derive a coupled system of equations for a and b.
result.transcription:
$p\frac{\partial^2 u}{\partial\beta^2}+q\frac{\partial u}{\partial\beta}=\frac{\partial u}{\partial t}$
$r\frac{\partial^2 u}{\partial\alpha\partial\beta}+s\frac{\partial u}{\partial\alpha}$
$\frac{\partial^2 u}{\partial\alpha^2}=0$
$\alpha\frac{\partial a}{\partial t}+\frac{\partial b}{\partial t}$
$\frac{\partial a}{\partial\beta}\alpha+\frac{\partial b}{\partial\beta}$
$\frac{\partial^2 a}{\partial\beta^2}\alpha+\frac{\partial^2 b}{\partial\beta^2}$
$\frac{\partial a}{\partial\beta}$ $\frac{\partial a}{\partial\alpha}a$[?]
$\frac{\partial^2 p}{\partial\alpha^2}\frac{\partial^2 u}{\partial\beta^2}+\frac{\partial^2 q}{\partial\alpha^2}\frac{\partial u}{\partial\beta}$
$2\frac{\partial p}{\partial\alpha}\frac{\partial^3 u}{\partial\beta^2\partial\alpha}+\left(2\frac{\partial q}{\partial\alpha}+\frac{\partial^2 r}{\partial\alpha^2}\right)\frac{\partial^2 u}{\partial\alpha\partial\beta}+\frac{\partial^2 s}{\partial\alpha^2}\frac{\partial u}{\partial\alpha}=0$

$\alpha=k\alpha'+s$
$\frac{\partial u}{\partial\alpha}d\alpha=k\,d\alpha'+\left(\alpha'\frac{\partial k}{\partial\beta}+\frac{\partial s}{\partial\beta}\right)d\beta$
$\frac{\partial u}{\partial\beta}d\beta=d\beta$
$\frac{\partial u}{\partial\beta}=\left(\frac{\partial u}{\partial\beta}\right)-\left(\alpha'\frac{\partial k}{\partial\beta}+\frac{\partial s}{\partial\beta}\right)\frac{1}{k}\frac{\partial u}{\partial\alpha'}$
$\frac{\partial u}{\partial\beta}$

[-$p=$-] [-$p=$-] $q=k\alpha+k_1$
$r=-k\alpha^2+[-2k\alpha-]m\alpha+n$
$s=l\alpha+q$

$(-k\alpha^2+m\alpha+n)[-(-2k\alpha+m)-]\frac{\partial a}{\partial\beta}+(l\alpha+q)a+p\left(\frac{\partial^2 a}{\partial\beta^2}\alpha+\frac{\partial^2 b}{\partial\beta^2}\right)+(k\alpha+k_1)\left(\frac{\partial a}{\partial\beta}\alpha+\frac{\partial b}{\partial\beta}\right)=\frac{\partial a}{\partial t}\alpha+\frac{\partial b}{\partial t}$

$\frac{\partial a}{\partial t}=k_1\frac{\partial a}{\partial\beta}+k\frac{\partial b}{\partial\beta}+p\frac{\partial^2 a}{\partial\beta^2}+la+m\frac{\partial a}{\partial\beta}$
$\frac{\partial b}{\partial t}=k_1[-\frac{\partial b}{\partial\beta}+\ldots-]\frac{\partial b}{\partial\beta}+qa+n\frac{\partial a}{\partial\beta}+p\frac{\partial^2 b}{\partial\beta^2}$

methods.what: Parabolic heat-type equation in β and t with coefficients p, q
Ansatz u linear in α (second α-derivative zero), u = aα + b
Condition from differentiating twice in α
Change of variable α = kα' + s and transformation of the β-derivative
Choice of coefficients polynomial in α
Resulting coupled system for a and b by comparing powers of α
methods.quote: $\frac{\partial a}{\partial t}=k_1\frac{\partial a}{\partial\beta}+k\frac{\partial b}{\partial\beta}+p\frac{\partial^2 a}{\partial\beta^2}+la+m\frac{\partial a}{\partial\beta}$
